stories.title: Should you read the code, is RAG dead, and did Skills kill MCP?
stories.snippet: We dive into these questions and other AI hot takes on the latest episode of the GitHub Podcast. The post Should you read the code, is RAG dead, and did Skills kill MCP? appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
stories.summary: The article explores five AI hot takes from the GitHub Podcast, arguing that the truth usually lies beneath surface-level controversy. It emphasizes that developers must still review AI-generated code, though the depth of review should match the risk and context of the change. Employers care more about AI judgment and clear explanations of workflow than total dependence or refusal. Skills and MCP serve different purposes—MCP provides standard interfaces for tools while skills offer context, process guidance, and best practices—so neither has replaced the other. RAG remains relevant because grounded retrieval helps models produce better, more accurate answers, and code that confuses AI often confuses human developers too, signaling a maintainability problem. The piece concludes that real experimentation and building produce more value than endless debate, citing Pollinations AI's credit-based contribution system and the Avian Visitors bird-listening e-ink display as examples.

stories.title: System One models like Jev can train their own replacements
stories.summary: System One models like Jev are fast, general-purpose classifiers that can be prompted for a wide variety of tasks, unlike traditional classifiers which require task-specific training and large datasets. Training bespoke classifiers remains beyond the skillset of most engineering teams, but Jev solves this by allowing any team to plug in a model with a simple prompt for specific tasks like deciding whether to notify a user about a Slack message. Although generic classifiers like Jev are larger and more expensive to run than specialized ones, it is easy to collect their input and output data once a prompt is working well. That collected data can then be used to train a cheaper, faster, hand-built classifier tailored to the specific task. The author expects this distillation pattern, of turning successful System One model usage into dedicated classifiers, to become common if such models take off.

stories.title: Grit your teeth and ship it
stories.summary: Being good at building and being good at shipping are two separate skills that often work against each other in the short term. Ira Glass famously noted that creative people have excellent taste but their early work doesn't yet match that taste, and the only solution is to ship anyway. Gifted programmers often resist shipping because flaws in their code bother them emotionally, causing them to freeze up, retreat to smaller safe tasks like tweaking dev environments, or spin in shame until they quit. The author applies the same principle to his writing, publishing blog posts he considers poorly-written because biasing toward shipping builds momentum. He observes that shipping gets easier with practice, and there's no correlation between which drafts he felt good about and which became popular with readers. As a result, producing a high volume of work yields better results than perfecting a small number of pieces, making it essential to be momentum-based rather than outcome-based.

stories.title: Migrating the GitHub Copilot runtime to Rust, using Copilot
stories.snippet: A rewrite this size wasn't affordable before agents. Here's what porting the Copilot agent runtime to 800,000 lines of production Rust actually took. The post Migrating the GitHub Copilot runtime to Rust, using Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
stories.summary: GitHub completely rewrote its Copilot agent runtime from TypeScript on Node.js into more than 800,000 lines of production Rust, with AI agents writing most of the code across 128 pull requests. The project, which would have required a whole team a year or two before agents, was completed primarily by a single developer in just a few months, while the rest of the team continued expanding the runtime's capabilities. The rewrite was motivated by performance problems caused by the original architecture, which intertwined the TUI and runtime and forced SDK consumers across six languages to spawn an out-of-process CLI hosting Node and V8, adding roughly 100 MB of working set per client. The new Rust runtime exposes a C ABI for clean in-process embedding, eliminating cross-process overhead. During the port, approximately 430,000 lines of TypeScript passed through the migration, and overall performance improved by orders of magnitude.

stories.title: Marketing ops as code: Automating events from planning to follow-up on GitHub
stories.snippet: If you can write down how you do your work, you can automate it. Here's what I did to support GitHub's APAC marketing team. The post Marketing ops as code: Automating events from planning to follow-up on GitHub appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
stories.summary: Tomoko Tanaka, who runs marketing for GitHub in Japan and Korea, automated her team's event workflows by handing runbooks to GitHub Copilot rather than writing code herself. The system is built on three GitHub primitives: issue forms capture event details, labels act as triggers, and GitHub Actions workflows execute the work once an event-setup label is applied, handling landing page duplication, UTM generation, invitation drafting, and project board updates. An AGENTS.md file guides Copilot on naming conventions and regional details during the planning conversation, while a DRY_RUN repository variable lets the team rehearse without touching external systems. Daily registration screening runs on a schedule, and invite-only events are filtered against defined criteria. Post-event work is handled by slash commands like /lead-upload and /event-report, which are GitHub Copilot agent skills defined as Markdown runbook files, keeping the system flexible across APAC's varied markets.

stories.summary: FAMOS is a feed-forward model designed to predict movable-part segmentation and joint parameters for articulated objects from a sparse, unordered set of partial point clouds. Unlike most feed-forward methods that infer articulation from a single observation and rely heavily on category-level shape priors, FAMOS jointly reasons over multiple observations while naturally supporting a variable number of inputs, including the single-view case. To aggregate articulation cues across observations, the authors introduce a Multi-state Articulation Transformer with alternating state-wise and global attention, along with an observed articulation span objective that encourages the model to leverage the full observation set by supervising each part's motion range. To address limitations in the scale and diversity of existing datasets, they also propose a procedural data generator that synthesizes self-annotated assets during training. Experiments on PartNet-Mobility, ACD, and ArtiCraft-10K demonstrate consistent improvements over both feed-forward and optimization-based baselines.

stories.title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
stories.snippet: Professional design requires any-color control: the ability to specify an object's target color with any 24-bit hex value for image generation and editing. Prior work has explored color generation, editing, and colorization, but often relies on dedicated color representations or specialized inference procedures. Advances in large language models offer a simpler starting point: even compact models can associate hex values with color semantics. stories.summary: Paint-Anything is a method that enables any-color control for image generation and editing by allowing users to specify object colors using 24-bit hex values. It learns a shared hex-prompt interface through object-level color supervision and is trained on Paint-500K, a dataset constructed from real images via object grounding, perceptual color labeling, and editing-pair synthesis. To address shadow-induced inaccuracy in real-image color labels, the authors incorporate pure-color anchors whose pixels exactly match their paired hex values, applied only at high-noise timesteps. The paper also introduces Any Color Benchmark (ACBench), comprising ACBench-T2I and ACBench-Edit, to evaluate object-level hex color fidelity. On FLUX.2-4B, Paint-Anything improves ACBench-T2I and ACBench-Edit scores by 85.3% and 28.3% respectively over the base model, while also achieving the highest average CompColor score among compared methods.

stories.title: Coding Agents with an Obstacle-Aware Harness for Safe Robot Manipulation
stories.snippet: Coding agents have emerged as a promising paradigm for robot manipulation: a language model writes the robot controller as a program, and agents built in this way now operate robots without robot-specific training.Whether this paradigm is also safe, however, has not been asked. We evaluate coding agent under a safety constraint, where each task pairs a manipulation goal with an obstacle the robot must not touch. The agent pursues the goal but collides with the obstacle in most cases, treating task completion as its sole objective while neglecting safety. The agent reasons about the obstacle in its traces, and the prompt already forbids touching it, so neither perception nor instruction is at fault; the fault lies in the planning, where the stated constraint never becomes a priority. stories.title: Workspace Models: Lightweight Robotic Memory via Saliency-Driven Supervision
stories.snippet: Complex robotic manipulation tasks frequently require a long-term memory of past events and actions. stories.title: ERCPMP-Gx: Endoscopic Image and Video Dataset for Morphological, Histopathological, and Genomic Characterization of Colorectal Polyposis
stories.snippet: Hereditary polyposis syndromes can be precursor lesions to colorectal cancer and are associated with a broad spectrum of extracolonic tumors. Early identification and accurate classification of these syndromes are essential for timely diagnosis, individualized patient management, and targeted surveillance strategies for affected families. stories.title: Laya on Mac M4 CoreML Offline
stories.summary: A GitHub Gist by fordnox shares a shell script for running Laya on a Mac M4 with CoreML offline support. The script creates a project directory, initializes a uv environment, installs the laya-coreml demo package, downloads a multilingual CoreML/ANE model from Hugging Face, and runs the laya-coreml-snake command. The author also posted a memory usage analysis using samply, showing the python3.12 process on macOS 27.0 ARM64 consumed 560.4M of physical memory with a peak of 778.0M. A comment by coezbek demonstrates using Laya through Cloudflare's API at laya.inference.zaitlabs.com, where a query about failing payouts returned a noul urgency score of 0.7894.

stories.title: Show HN: An e-ink frame that hears birds and draws them as 1800s illustrations
stories.snippet: See also: Avian Visitors - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48343424 - May 2026 (20 comments)
stories.summary: Fugleramme is an open-source e-ink frame that detects birds by audio in real time and renders them as hand-curated 1800s-style natural-history illustrations on an Inky Impression 13.3" panel connected to a Raspberry Pi 5. It pairs with BirdNET-Go, which uses a microphone and local AI to classify species; Fugleramme polls the API, matches each species to an illustration, and repacks the page only when the bird list changes. The artwork includes over 800 cut-outs from public-domain Scandinavian, British, and central European plates covering more than 400 species, with birds sized by body mass and placed on a textured paper background, while no detections shows a bare perch. The frame can run without the e-ink panel as a web-only kiosk and can be installed via a script on a Raspberry Pi or in a Docker container. Released under the MIT license, a live version currently runs from a kitchen window in Bergen, Norway.

stories.title: I turned Jev into a (lousy) chatbot
stories.summary: jevchat is a tool that turns Jev into a chatbot by asking it at every step which symbol should come next, drawing from a normalised probability distribution over an alphabet that can include letters, BPE tokens, or whole words. It supports several sampling strategies—choice, bisect, buckets, and refine—and two presentation modes: "symbol," where Jev judges bare options, and "hypothesis," where it judges the resulting completed strings, which the author found roughly triples top-1 accuracy and doubles the probability mass on the right symbol for character alphabets. The project was implemented by Claude based on the author's descriptions of the algorithms. Installation uses Poetry with a git-ignored .env file holding the API key, and a command-line interface supports interactive chat with commands like /alphabet, /temp, and /reset, as well as a one-shot ask command. The interface shows the reply streaming in with live statistics on generation rate and top-scoring symbols, and Ctrl-C cancels mid-generation. Beam search is also available, and the project includes 158 offline tests using mocked clients, with only the bench command hitting the real API.

stories.title: AI-generated posters don’t have to be horrible
stories.summary: AI-generated posters often share a repetitive, identikit style that has become irritating through overexposure. The author set out to demonstrate that AI tools like ChatGPT can produce more distinctive designs when prompted with specific aesthetic directions. By requesting styles such as Bauhaus/modernist, risograph print, Memphis Design, Japanese minimal, brutalist, and 90s rave flyer aesthetics, the author generated a varied series of posters that stood out from typical village fayre templates. Naming a specific design movement or style proved to be an effective strategy for avoiding the default AI look. The author acknowledges the posters still retain some AI characteristics, but argues they are distinctive and visually appealing rather than derivative. Inspired by the experiment, the author compiled a catalogue of one hundred poster styles with ready-to-paste prompts and example images for each.

stories.title: I built non-autoregressive decision models with RL a year ago
stories.summary: The author spent months building non-autoregressive decision models trained with reinforcement learning, publishing an arXiv paper and open-source weights in March 2025, followed by a second paper in September 2025. Frustrated when TypeSafe AI launched Jev in September 2026 as a proprietary version of the same concept, they developed Laya, a fully open-source Apache 2.0 alternative running in 32.8 milliseconds on a single GPU—6 to 8 times faster than Jev. Laya supports three decision primitives (choice, score, noul) across three specialized checkpoints, including a multilingual model covering 100+ languages. A built-in Router inspects Unicode scripts before inference, since the English-only model catastrophically fails on non-Latin scripts while falsely reporting high confidence. Benchmarks show Laya beating Jev on typed-decisions, AG News, and DAIR Emotion tasks, with 3x better calibration error, though the author openly acknowledges accuracy degrades on choice questions with more than 20 options.

stories.title: Two parallel neural ectoderm progenitors contribute to the developing brain
stories.summary: Stanford Medicine researchers have overturned the long-held view that the brain develops from a single progenitor cell, demonstrating that it instead arises from two separate neural ectoderm populations running in parallel from the earliest stages of embryonic development. The forebrain and midbrain originate from cells expressing the gene Otx2, while the hindbrain forms from cells expressing Gbx2, with the two populations showing fundamentally different chromatin configurations that lock each into its fate. This explains why scientists struggled for decades to grow hindbrain neurons in the lab, and enabled the team to successfully generate functional hindbrain motor neurons from human pluripotent stem cells for the first time. The same dual-origin pattern appears in chickens, zebrafish, and acorn worms, indicating the two nervous systems evolved independently over 550 million years before being packaged together. The findings open new avenues for studying diseases affecting the brain stem, including spinal muscular atrophy, ALS, and the hunger-regulating circuits targeted by drugs like semaglutide.
